questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted somewhere with good academic opportunities combined with a vibrant social life, which I very much found to be the case.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Highly recommend

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall okay, make sure to research a bit about the places where you can find the relevant information, but both the people at UCPH and UC Berkeley were happy to help. I would also highly suggest seeking advice among the other people how either have gone or are going to the same destination.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly emails about the relevant events from the central office, although I gennerally found information for exchange students to be lacking. Often we were being lumped together with American transfer students who did not always face the same questions and problems.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Be prepared to not know everything in the beginning, everyone is trying their best to have everyone informed but sometimes it will take some time before you know all the relevant information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: START APPLYING EARLY! I cannot stress this enough. I lived in one of the coops which was a wonderful experience (although a bit dirty) but that was only because I applied as soon as I knew where I was going for my exchange. You have very decent odds of finding housing if you start early be that I-House, coops, AirBnBs, or other apartments but the opportunities quickly disappear as time passes. Do not wait until a few weeks before your exchange to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There isn't really much on campus housing so you will probably be living off campus which is completely fine. You will also likely have to share with other people sometimes also sharing rooms. If you can get over that fact it's a great way to meet new people and find some friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's easy once you know how to do it, but there is very little information on how to navigate their portal, take some time to browse through their endless website to scavenge for that information if you're in doubt.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After creating your login you can access the regestration site. Here you can browse through the available courses and build your class schedule which while a little complicated is actually super nice once you learn how to use it. Once you have build your schedule you can save that. You will then have a specific date where registration opens and you can get your preferred classes. I did not find it hard to get in to my classes as I applied early but spots fill up relatively quickly. Also REMEMBER TO CHECK YOUR EXAMS as they are all crammed into one week they may overlap, so be prepared with alternatives.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A few emails were sent out, but you can find people explaining it on YouTube as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted but found out two of them had overlapping exams, so I later had to switch one of them out, which was not a problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to sign up as early as possible if you have a class that is very important to you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All the courses were upper division undergraduate courses the level was very similar to UCPH courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Gennerally it's similar. You do, though, have significantly less time spent in small classes/sections - often only one hour for every 3 hours of lecture meaning that the instructor/GSI has way less time to cover the material that the lecturer has covered in lecturer. This means more studying by yourself, so be prepared for that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Game Theory in the Social Sciences
Industrial Organization and Public Policy
Public Economics
The Chinese Economy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the courses were good, I was particularly happy with Industrial Organization as the professor was really engaged in the material and had good sense of humor - although it was also the hardest course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is expensive, so while I had food included in my housing I easily spend a lot on that especially because you have to tip everywhere.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buses are free (in the Berkeley area) which was amazing but food was expensive and also renting a car if you plan on day tripping.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is an incredible amount of clubs, sports etc. I highly recommend joining one or more as it's a great way to meet new people. They have several events where they advertise the various clubs (and there is a club for almost everything imaginable) and are very open to new comers.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a club for almost everything, chess, soccer, quidditch, political groups, ball room dancing, music, journalism, entrepreneurship, basket ball and so much more. They have a dedicated day where all the clubs assemble on one of the plazas and you can hear more about them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As mentioned clubs are a great way to meet people, I also suggest attending some of the many activities hosted for both exchange students as well as all students in general. While some may be more interesting than others they are a great way to meet people especially in the first weeks.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Remember to set money aside to go on weekend road trips. California is full of amazing nature e.g. Highway 1/Big Sur, Yosemite, Lake Tahoe, Sierra Nevada and so on. It's also relatively cheap to fly to amazing places such as San Diego, Mexico, Hawaii and Las Vegas.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found Americans to be very open and talkative. The cultural differences aren't huge and people are generally happy to engage with you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As I said, joining clubs, attending university organized events, Taco Tuesdays are a big thing, even starting conversations with people in your classes can lead to unexpected socializing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of people at Berkeley are really ambitious and have busy schedules meaning that organizing hangouts can sometimes be a hassle.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How easy going and talkative Americans are. They are very easy to make friends with if you make the effort.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to new experiences and people, you're almost guaranteed to have a fun time.
Be prepared to be a bit confused/overwhelmed in the beginning as information is lacking.
Go on several weekend/holiday trips, California is amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that it's way easier to change classes after registration at Berkeley compared to UCPH so if your schedule is causing trouble or the class is not working for some reason research other cases you can swap it for (off course while checking that it works with your studies back home)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I got and the trips I went on.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the midterms/exams are in hand. If you're not used to handwriting be prepared for that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
